title: Frontend: Focus Input
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Focus Input. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Render a labelled Message input and a Focus message button. Clicking the button focuses the input without changing its value. Show [data-testid="focused"] yes while focused, no on blur.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep a DOM ref with useRef, attach it to the input, and call focus in the event handler.
alternativeApproaches: Focus the first invalid input after form submission without fighting a user’s current typing position.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Focus button activation; input absent; disabled input.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
